question: Which statement best describes Class fields and methods?
options: A class groups typed data (fields) and behavior (methods). Fields are declared with a name and type and may have initializers; methods are functions whose parameters and return types are checked. TypeScript verifies every field is assigned before use and that method calls match their signatures.

public (default) members are accessible anywhere; private members only within the declaring class; protected members within the class and its subclasses. readonly allows assignment only at declaration or in the constructor. These are compile-time checks enforced by TypeScript, not runtime enforcement.

A class can declare implements to promise it conforms to one or more interfaces. The compiler then checks the class provides every required member with compatible types. implements is purely a contract — it adds no behavior and is erased from the output.

Prefixing a constructor parameter with an access modifier (public, private, protected, or readonly) declares and assigns a field in one step. This shorthand removes the boilerplate of declaring a field and then assigning this.x = x in the constructor body.
